answer: Give each applicant one garden plot fed by a metered glacier stream. The gardener fits a 40 dollar meter on the tap and logs water and harvest weekly for 90 days. Two neighbors walk the plot monthly and sign each entry, while the readings go to a ledger that flags use without a harvest. Forging 10,000 plots would freeze 1,000,000 tokens and cost 400,000 dollars in meters, and the ledger would spot the ripple of identical times on plots that never grew a tomato. Like a glacier feeding a garden, slow verified water grows roots, and a dry plot with perfect paperwork loses its tap.
